reviewer_scope: Independent code/representation review; this agent authored audit documents and retained-ligand matrix runner, not production code or regression tests.
conclusion: No unresolved blocking defect found in the reviewed atom-identity mapping change. Results remain software equivalence evidence, not scientific force-field accuracy validation.

findings.issue: An atom map could cover all native indices while pairing one index with a different symmetric template atom name.
findings.resolution: Constructor now requires each template atom position to equal its recorded native index and rejects malformed fields and boolean/noninteger indices.

reviewed_invariants: Identity is selected by recorded chain, residue id, insertion code and residue name.
Atom names, counts, elements, native/template indices, internal connectivity and absence of external ligand bonds are validated.
Generated DML templates cannot silently fall back to graph-only matching when no declared binding exists.
An explicit template selection cannot bypass the identity map.
Ligand parameterization writes a complete heavy+hydrogen mapping; prepared bundle loading uses it at downstream assembly.
Legacy atom mappings are reconstructed only when saved heavy-atom indices, hydrogen count and XML element ordering support the prior documented naming convention.
Existing native energy and force thresholds are unchanged.
limitations: The adapter overrides two private OpenMM hooks; version changes require these integration regressions. Upstream signatures and implementation fingerprints are recorded in review-upstream-source.json.
The supplied mapping is provenance, not an external chemical identity oracle; valid mapping/force agreement does not validate protonation, tautomer choice or physical force-field accuracy.
Retained fixture coverage is representative and finite. This change does not add support for arbitrary covalent ligands, unsupported metals, or arbitrary unusual residue templates.
